hours.text: We're open Monday to Saturday, from 7 in the morning at Indiranagar and until 9 at night at Nagarbhavi, Jayanagar and Whitefield, with a short lunch break from 2 to 2:30. Each doctor has their own hours, and we're closed on Sundays.

pricing_policy.text: Prices depend on the tooth and the treatment, so I'll give you the usual range, and before anything starts you get a written estimate, so there are no surprises.

insurance_policy.text: We don't do cashless insurance. Most health policies only cover dental work after an accident or a hospital stay, but if your plan has an OPD or dental benefit, we give you itemised bills and reports the same day so you can claim it back.

escalation.text: The doctor can go through that with you at your visit.

facts.text: A consultation or check-up is 400 rupees, and it's adjusted against any treatment you start that day.
A cleaning is usually between 1,000 and 1,500 rupees.
A filling is usually 1,000 to 2,500 rupees, depending on the size and the material.
A root canal is usually 5,000 to 8,000 rupees per tooth, and a crown afterwards is extra, from about 4,000.

A simple extraction is usually 1,000 to 2,000 rupees. A wisdom tooth that needs minor surgery is usually 3,000 to 8,000, depending on how it's placed; Dr Ali, our oral surgeon at Whitefield, does those.

Metal braces are usually 30,000 to 50,000 rupees for the full treatment, and tooth-coloured ceramic ones 45,000 to 70,000. It takes about 12 to 24 months with a short check every month, and there's a no-cost EMI option.

Clear aligners start at about 70,000 rupees, and Invisalign is usually between one and two and a half lakh, depending on how much correction is needed. Dr Iyer at Indiranagar does them, and there's a no-cost EMI option.
A children's visit is usually 400 to 600 rupees.
In-clinic whitening is usually 6,000 to 12,000 rupees and takes about an hour in one visit. We check your teeth first, because whitening doesn't change the colour of crowns or fillings.

An implant with its crown is usually 30,000 to 55,000 rupees per tooth, depending on the implant brand and whether bone support is needed. It takes two or three visits over about three months, and Dr Nair at Jayanagar and Dr Ali at Whitefield do them.
You can pay by UPI, any debit or credit card, net banking or cash, with no extra charge.
For treatments over about 10,000 rupees, like braces, aligners, implants or crowns, there's a no-cost EMI over three to twelve months through our finance partner, and credit card EMI works too.
Just bring any old X-rays or prescriptions, and a list of any medicines you take.

facts.topic: how long the first visit takes
facts.text: A first visit takes about 30 to 45 minutes, including the check-up and an X-ray if it's needed.
We see children of all ages; a parent just needs to come along for anyone under 18.

facts.topic: how many visits a root canal takes
facts.text: A root canal usually takes two or three visits of about an hour each.
All our branches take digital X-rays of single teeth right there, with very low radiation, and the full-mouth OPG X-ray is done at Indiranagar or Jayanagar.
Treatments are done under local anaesthetic, so you feel pressure but not pain, and the doctor checks in with you throughout. There's usually mild soreness for a day or two afterwards.
All instruments are sterilised after every patient, and we use disposables wherever we can.
There's no fee to cancel or move an appointment, just let us know.
If you're in a lot of pain or have swelling, we keep same-day slots for emergencies and we'll fit you in today.
Walk-ins are welcome, but booking ahead means you won't have to wait.
Our team speaks English, Kannada and Hindi, and between our doctors we also speak Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, Marathi, Tulu and Urdu.

Pearl Dental has four branches in Bengaluru, at Nagarbhavi, Indiranagar, Jayanagar and Whitefield, with eight doctors, including specialists for root canals, braces and aligners, children, crowns and dentures, and oral surgery. We do everything from check-ups and cleanings to implants.
I can tell you about our clinic, the services we offer, our doctors, prices and timings, and book, change or cancel appointments.

A crown, or cap, is usually 4,000 to 8,000 rupees for a metal-ceramic one, and 9,000 to 15,000 for zirconia, which looks the most natural. It takes two visits about a week apart; Dr Nair at Jayanagar is our crown and denture specialist.

Yes, we make dentures. A full denture is usually 10,000 to 18,000 rupees per jaw, and a partial one 5,000 to 15,000, depending on the material. It takes four or five short visits over two to three weeks, with Dr Nair at Jayanagar.
An X-ray of a single tooth is about 250 rupees, done right there at any branch. A full-mouth OPG X-ray is about 800, at our Indiranagar and Jayanagar branches.

For children, a fluoride coating is about 800 to 1,000 rupees, and sealants, which protect the back teeth from cavities, are about 800 to 1,200 per tooth. Dr Kulkarni at Jayanagar and Dr Reddy at Whitefield do them in a short visit.

Gum treatment starts with a deep cleaning, usually 1,500 to 2,500 rupees per section of the mouth; most people need two to four sections, done over one or two visits. Bleeding or swollen gums are the usual first sign, and it's very treatable when caught early.

After an extraction, bite on the gauze for about 30 minutes, then stick to soft, cool food like curd or idli for a day or two. Avoid straws, spitting, smoking and spicy food for 24 hours, and don't rinse hard on the first day.

A little oozing for a day after an extraction is normal. Fold some clean gauze or cotton, bite on it firmly for 20 to 30 minutes and keep your head raised. If it's still bleeding heavily after that, come straight in, or go to the nearest hospital emergency if we're closed.
After a filling, wait until the numbness wears off before eating, usually two hours, and avoid very hard or sticky food that day. After a root canal, chew on the other side until the crown is fitted.
facts.topic: care after a filling or root canal

facts.text: Most people go straight back to work the same day; after an extraction or a wisdom tooth it's best to rest that day, and after implant surgery a day or two.

We suggest a child's first visit around the first birthday or when the first tooth comes in, then a check-up every six months, and a braces check around age seven. Dr Kulkarni at Jayanagar and Dr Reddy at Whitefield are great with children.

We see a lot of senior patients, for dentures, check-ups and gum care. Bring their medicine list, and someone can come in with them; for a wheelchair, Indiranagar is on the ground floor and Jayanagar and Whitefield have lifts.

We treat patients with diabetes, BP, heart conditions and on blood thinners every day. Tell the doctor at the start, and bring your medicine list and recent sugar or BP readings; don't stop any medicine on your own, because the treatment is planned around it.

Check-ups and cleanings are safe during pregnancy, and the middle three months are the best time for any treatment that's needed. We only take an X-ray if it's really needed, with a lead apron, so just tell us how far along you are.

Sensitivity to cold or sweet things is very common, usually from worn enamel, receding gums or a small cavity. A sensitivity toothpaste helps mild cases, and a check-up finds the cause; the fix is often a quick filling or a protective coating in one visit.

A wisdom tooth that hurts or is coming in sideways is usually taken out. Dr Ali, our oral surgeon at Whitefield, does it under local anaesthetic in about 30 to 45 minutes; it's usually 3,000 to 8,000 rupees, and most people rest for a day.
Of course, we're happy to give a second opinion; just bring any X-rays and the treatment plan you were given, and the consultation is 400 rupees.
There's usually a short follow-up a week after treatment at no charge, and we recommend a check-up and cleaning every six months.
Yes, you can have copies of your X-rays, reports and prescriptions; just ask at the front desk and we'll share them the same day, on WhatsApp or printed.
Crowns come with a warranty of five years for metal-ceramic and ten years for zirconia, and implants carry the manufacturer's warranty on the implant itself; you get it in writing with your estimate.
Before any treatment starts you get a written estimate with every step and its cost, so there are no hidden charges.

When we're closed, for pain you can take the painkiller you normally use and hold a cold pack on the cheek, then call us when we open; we keep same-day slots for emergencies. If swelling spreads to the eye or neck, or you have trouble breathing or swallowing, go to the nearest hospital emergency.
facts.topic: what to do when the clinic is closed

facts.text: If swelling is spreading to your eye or neck, you have trouble breathing or swallowing, a high fever with swelling, or bleeding that won't stop after 30 minutes of pressure, please go to the nearest hospital emergency or call 108 right away.
Besides check-ups, cleanings, fillings, root canals, extractions, braces and children's dentistry, we also do crowns, dentures, gum treatment, implants, wisdom teeth, whitening and clear aligners.

Yes, we see whole families: Dr Kulkarni and Dr Reddy for children, our general dentists for adults, and dentures and gum care for parents and grandparents. You can book everyone on the same day, one after the other.

Our doctors include MDS specialists for root canals, braces, children, crowns and dentures, and oral surgery, each with seven to fifteen years' experience. Every instrument is sterilised after each patient, and you get a written estimate before any treatment.
facts.topic: about the clinic and doctors' experience

facts.text: Indiranagar is on the ground floor, and Jayanagar and Whitefield have lifts, so they're all easy with a wheelchair or walker. Nagarbhavi is on the first floor by stairs only.
